title: Review (Supported for S, I, X, D; E not checked) of the hunting-predator ecology on fresh seed 54 at 256^2: prey crash 61 -> 4 when predators arrive and recover to 50 against a static twin (63-75); 21 persistent predator-only splits, generation 2, seen as rods pinching in random strips
summary: Re-ran the claimed world at 256^2 on seed 54 with its predator-free twin and tracked each species channel alone. Prey fall from 61 to 4 within 1000 t of the predators' arrival, recover to 50 by t 6100 and fall to 13-19, while the twin is a static emulsion growing to 75; predators hold 52-72 bodies, make 21 persistent splits (generation 2, no re-merges, 10 right after touching prey), and random strips show rods and Y-shapes pinching into persisting droplets. Prey make no persistent splits when predators are present. The fuel fork for E was not run.

observations.S: rerun/seed54/sheet.png t=0 smoothed noise; predator noise added over the domain at t=2000
observations.I: rerun/seed54/sheet.png: discrete prey condensates and predator droplets, 52-72 predators to t=12000 (species_track.py)
observations.D: species_track.py on the predator channel: 21 persistent splits, generation 2, 0 re-merges; strips_pred_s54.png rows 2-4 rods pinching into two droplets that persist >= 500 t

seeds_run.result: pass for S, I, X, D (predators); one prey crash-recovery-decline, prey make no persistent splits with predators

controls_run.X: twin256/seed54 (pred_on 0, same seed, grid, duration, lineage window)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed at 256^2. Counts on rendered frames 100 t apart at c > 0.5. I saw one prey crash and recovery, not repeated cycles. D holds for predators; prey do not divide when predators are present. Predators are seeded as noise at t=2000. E (fuel fork) not run by me.
